name: Metalwood Studio

picks.title: Metal Logo 5-Panel Hat
picks.why: TGI calls the Metal Logo 5-Panel 'the signature hat of the brand' (unstructured 5-panel with the metal logo), offered in several colorways.

picks.title: Tri-Metal T-Shirt
picks.why: TGI names the Tri-Metal Tee the entry point to the brand, with a crest graphic drawing on the medieval heraldry and industrial signage that runs through Metalwood's design.

picks.title: Mechanic Jacket
picks.why: TGI's Take calls the $278 Mechanic Jacket 'the argument' for the brand; it is the most expensive piece in TGI's edit (store: 100% melton wool, 2-way zip, metal charm at back neck).

alternates.title: Bomber Jacket
alternates.why: TGI names the Bomber Jacket one of the two statement outerwear pieces (store: custom Metalwood trim, embroidered details, leopard-print pocket gusset).

alternates.title: Metal Logo Torque Wrench
alternates.why: A divot tool shaped like a torque wrench, which TGI calls 'the most on-brand object Metalwood makes'.

notes: The Metal Logo 5-Panel in Navy (the colourway TGI featured) is sold out, as are Black, Brown and Real Leaf Camo; Spruce, White and Fatigue Green are in stock, so Spruce is used. The Medieval Terry Polo and World Class Zip Polo TGI featured no longer resolve on the store. TGI described the Mechanic Jacket as waxed cotton, but the store lists 100% melton wool, so TGI's post may need correcting. Bomber also in Seafoam (TGI's colourway; only XL/XXL left). The adidas x Metalwood MC70 shoe ($200, in stock) is left out because it is a collab. Some sizes are sold out on every pick (Tri-Metal L/XL, Mechanic XL/XXL, Bomber S).
